svg.text: Band-edge adjacent-power relief clears the settle shelf before the residual gap
Hold loop gain fixed at 0.020. Lower adjacent power restores the threshold metric quickly, but the half-sine residual ranking survives much longer.

text.tspan: Same SRRC QPSK setup, same 63-tap band-edge filters, same 96-symbol loop update, same 1.20–1.30 R_s nearby-spacing band. This pass freezes loop gain at 0.020 and moves only adjacent relative power. The question is
whether making the adjacent channel weaker turns the settle-shelf return into a real catch-up instead of just a cleaner threshold read.

svg.text: A stronger adjacent pushes the first full settle point later

text.tspan: At +3 dB, the half-sine lane is still not fully settled at 1.24 R_s:
its tail fraction is only 0.000, and the first full-settle point moves
out to 1.30 R_s instead of the 0 dB baseline at 1.24 R_s.

svg.text: A modest relief already clears the whole threshold shelf

text.tspan: At -3 dB, every tested spacing from 1.20 through 1.30 R_s is fully
settled. The 1.20 R_s cell jumps from 0.000 at 0 dB to 1.000.

svg.text: But the residual ranking does not vanish with that relief

text.tspan: At -3 dB, the half-sine / proxy mean-tail residual ratio is still 8.8x
at 1.20 R_s, 13.4x at 1.24 R_s, and 34.1x at 1.30 R_s. Even at -9 dB,
the 1.24 R_s ratio still sits at 8.4x.

svg.text: Half-sine settle fraction at fixed gain 0.020

text.tspan: Each cell is the share of the last eight loop blocks inside ±0.05 R_s. Lower adjacent power

svg.text: the threshold shelf survives 0 dB, shifts later at +3 dB, and is already fully open across the band by 1.20 R_s at -3 dB.

text.tspan: This is the mean tail residual CFO ratio. Bigger means the half-sine lane still tracks less
cleanly than the proxy lane even after the threshold metric looks healthy.

svg.text: lower adjacent power cools the ratio, but it stays far above 1x across this grid.

text.tspan: Weaker adjacent power shifts the whole ratio family downward, but the curves still stay far
above parity. The settle shelf clears long before the ranking disappears.

svg.text: the whole family stays above 1x; weaker adjacent power helps, but it does not turn the nearby band into a residual crossover.

text.tspan: This is the direct mean tail-residual difference (half-sine minus proxy). The gap really does
shrink with weaker adjacent power. It just never flips sign in this bounded pass.

svg.text: adjacent-power relief is real; the absolute gap cools a lot, but it never flips sign here.
Bounded pass: gain = 0.020, settle threshold = ±0.05 R_s, tail = last 8 loop blocks, adjacent power sweep = +3 to -9 dB.
